title: In Vitro Permeation of FITC-loaded Ferritins Across a Rat Blood-brain Barrier: a Model to Study the Delivery of Nanoformulated Molecules
protocol: Coat cell culture flasks with poly-L-lysine 100 μg/ml (1 hr at RT) or fibronectin 50 μg/ml (1 hr at 37 °C).
Thaw 1 x 10^6 RCAs and 5 x 10^5 RBMECs in Endothelial Cell Medium supplemented with 5% fetal bovine serum, 1% endothelial cell growth supplement, and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Seed RCAs in a T175 flask with 20 ml sECM.
Seed RBMECs in a T75 flask with 10 ml sECM.
Maintain cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in a humidified atmosphere for approximately 6 days.
Detach cells using trypsin-EDTA solution (trypsin 1:250) for 5 min.
Stop trypsin activity with sECM (2:1).
Centrifuge cell suspensions at 750 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend the pellets in 60 ml sECM.
Split RBMECs into 3 T175 flasks and culture in sECM for another 3 days before seeding onto inserts.
Count total number of living RCAs by observing a cell suspension diluted 1:1 with trypan blue under an optical microscope in a Burker chamber.

Treat one side of the Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) membrane of 6 multi-well transparent inserts with poly-L-lysine 100 µg/ml and the other side with fibronectin 50 µg/ml to allow attachment of RCAs and BMECs.
Handle the inserts with tweezers to avoid contact with the PET membrane.
Place the inserts into a 6 well plate.
Add fibronectin solution (minimum 500 µl) into the upper chamber.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 hr.
Remove fibronectin solution after incubation.
Take the inserts off the multi-well plate and put them upside down on the bottom of a 150 cm2 Petri dish.
Gently add 800 µl of poly-L-lysine onto the bottom side of the insert and keep the solution on the inserts for 1 hour at room temperature.
Aspirate the poly-L-lysine solution and let the inserts dry at room temperature for 15-30 minutes.
Seed RCAs (35,000/cm²) onto the bottom side of the poly-L-lysine-coated inserts by dropping 800 µl of cell suspension onto the upside-down insert.
Leave the RCA suspension on the inserts for 4 hours at room temperature to allow efficient attachment of cells to the membrane.
Aspirate any residual solution, place the inserts into wells containing 2 ml of sECM and maintain the multi-well plate at 37°C and 5% CO₂ in a humidified atmosphere.
Change the sECM every 2 days for 3 days until RCAs have coated the lower face of the insert.
Seed RBMECs onto the upper side of the insert following subsequent steps.
Seed RBMECs onto the upper surface of the insert in sECM at a density of 60,000/cm².
Leave three inserts with astrocytes only to serve as TEER background.
Place the multi-well plate under standard culture conditions.
Maintain the system for at least 3 days, changing the sECM in both inner and lower chambers every 2 days.
On the 3rd day of co-culture, measure the TEER by placing inserts into a chamber filled with 4 ml of sECM.
Connect to an epithelial tissue volt/ohmmeter for TEER measurement.
Subtract the TEER values from RCAs-bearing inserts when recording BBB values.
Multiply resulting TEER values by the surface area of the insert (4.2 cm²) for expression in Ω x cm².
Measure TEER daily starting from the 3rd day of co-culture until stability is achieved, usually between the 5th and 7th day.
Once TEER values remain stable for at least two consecutive days, proceed to further validation or trans-BBB experiments.
Operate under sterile conditions.
Add 1 mg/ml FD40 (diluted in sECM) into the upper compartment of the BBBs.
Withdraw 200 μl sECM from the lower chamber after 1, 2 and 3 hours.
Measure the fluorescence intensity by spectrofluorimeter (λex 488 nm, λem 515 nm, slit 5).
Obtain values for sECM background fluorescence by measuring 500 μl of virgin medium using the same analytical parameters.
Subtract the sECM background fluorescence from all FD40 fluorescence values.
Determine the amount of permeated FD40 by comparison with a calibration curve produced with known concentrations (i.e., 0.312, 0.625, 1.25, 2.5 μg/ml) dissolved in sECM.
Calculate the apparent permeability coefficient (Papp) from the mean flux values according to Papp = J/AC.
Measure the FITC-FnN flux from the upper to the lower chamber of validated BBB models, compared to that of free dye after 7 and 24 hr of incubation.
Add FITC-FnN (50 µg/ml FnN, 1.1 µM FITC) or an equal amount of free FITC into the upper chamber of at least 6 BBB systems for each formulation.
Withdraw 2 ml of sECM solution from the lower chamber of at least 3 inserts after 7 hr.
Withdraw 2 ml of sECM solution from the lower chamber of other 3 inserts after 24 hr.
Measure the fluorescence intensity of 500 µl of collected samples by spectrofluorimeter (λex 488 nm, λem 515 nm, slit 5).
Obtain sECM background fluorescence by measuring 500 µl of medium using the same analytical parameters.
Subtract sECM background fluorescence from all FITC or FITC-FnN fluorescence values.

Determine the concentration of permeated FITC or FITC-FnN by comparing obtained fluorescence values with calibration curves produced with known concentrations of free or nanoformulated dye dissolved in 500 µl sECM.
Remove sECM from the upper chamber of BBB systems.
Wash inserts with PBS.
Fix RBMECs on at least two inserts for each experimental group by adding 500 µl paraformaldehyde (4% in phosphate buffer saline-PBS) to the upper compartment for 10 min at RT.
Wash inserts three times with PBS to remove residual paraformaldehyde.
Permeabilize RBMECs with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS for 10 minutes.
Perform a blocking step for 1 hr at RT with a solution containing 2% bovine serum albumin (BSA), 2% goat serum in PBS.
Incubate samples with an anti-Von Willebrand Factor (VWF) at 1:20 dilution, for 2 hr at RT.
Expose cells for 2 hours at room temperature to a solution containing secondary antibody at a 1:300 dilution and DAPI at a 1:1500 dilution in a buffer of 2% BSA and 2% goat serum.
Mount the insert pieces onto microscope slides using an antifade mounting solution.
Close the sample with a cover slip.
Analyze by confocal microscopy using an oil immersion lens at 40X magnification, 1.5 zoom, and 1,024 x 1,024 pixel resolution.
